LESSON: SOUND

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Natural Environment 2.2 Soil (8 Lessons) By the end of the sub-strand, the learn
Topic 2.3: Sound
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sound, part of Natural Environment 2.2 Soil (8 Lessons) By the end of the sub-strand, the learn in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do animals and other objects in our environment produce sounds? 2. Why are some sounds important in our lives?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sound together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: Learning independently is developed as learners take a walk in the immediate environment to identify various

sounds/ vibrations/ signals.

● Digital literacy: Creating with technology is developed as learners record audios or videos on various sounds/ signals.

● Self-efficacy: The skill of making observations is developed as learners identify sounds/vibrations/signals used to alert us to dangerous

situations.

Values:
● Responsibility: Learners enhance diligence while engaging in sound walk and taking turns while doing activities.

● Patriotism: Learners enrich loyalty as they obey laws and regulation on sounds that alert us on dangers for appropriate response.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Disaster risk reduction: Learners develop safety skills as they share information on limiting harmful effects of loud sounds.

Link to other Learning Areas:

● Language activities: Sounds in the immediate environment can be used to develop the skill of attentive listening.

Suggested Learning Resources

Adapted learner’s book, immediate environment, digital devices, hearing aids, animals, machines, humans, captioned and signed audio

visual clips,
